column2: req_desc

Create a stay by keyboard.
With `N` pressed from any control in `Reservation timeline`, the clerk tabs through `New stay` with focus wrapping inside it, presses Enter on `Create stay`, hears the result in `Desk notices`, sees the new block on the timeline and gets focus back on the opener.

Exact nightly pricing.
Every night of a stay is priced in whole cents by the published steps and one half-up rounding, matching each worked example in Business rules in the quote, the `Nightly breakdown` table, `Stay total` and every posted line.

Tax rates from a stated date.
The owner enters a new percentage with a start date after the business date, after which each night shows the rate in force on that night and earlier nights keep the old rate on the folio, invoice and reports.

One stay per create.
A double press of `Create stay` and a replay of the same `Idempotency-Key` yield one stay, one folio and one check-in email, and the same key with a different body is refused as published in Business rules.

Stay nights and overlaps.
A stay holds arrival up to but not including departure, so a same-day turnover fits one room, and the server refuses any overlap on create and on extend.

New stay field errors.
Invalid `New stay` input is refused with the published field messages and shows `Form errors` whose links move focus to each field, with nothing saved.

Keyboard room move.
With `M` pressed from any control in `Reservation timeline` the clerk picks up the current stay, places it with the arrow keys, hears each placement, drops it with Enter and hears the published move notice in `Desk notices`, and a drop that shifts a booked stay's dates keeps its length and reprices as published in Business rules.

Cancel a pick-up.
Escape during a pick-up returns the block to its old place with nothing sent to the server and announces the published cancelled notice in `Desk notices`.

Refused drop on an occupied room.
A move onto an occupied night is refused by the server with the published text in `Desk notices`, the block returns to its old place, and the message survives every repaint and live update that follows.

Stay panel keeps the newest state.
Reopening `Stay` during its closing motion leaves it open after the clock advances, and acting again during a pending stay or folio request keeps the newest state and the last message shown.

Published timeline attributes.
`Reservation timeline` carries the published row, column, cell and block attributes and the `Free rooms` region, and these reflect server state after every change and reload.

Last room goes to one clerk.
Of two simultaneous requests for one room's last free nights exactly one creates a stay and the other is refused with the published text, leaving one stay, one folio and one check-in email.

Two clerks, one notice.
Two front desk browsers take the last room or move one stay at once, the winner sees success, and the loser sees the published conflict notice in `Desk notices` with the screen showing the latest state.

Free room count stays live.
`Free rooms` shows the business date's free rooms and changes on every signed-in staff screen within the published live delay after a stay or room change.

Check-in guarded by room status.
Check-in succeeds only for a booked stay arriving on the business date in a clean or inspected room, and any other attempt gets its published refusal with the stay unchanged.

Housekeeper changes reach the desk live.
A housekeeper's tap on a phone changes the room chip on a desk browser without reload, and the desk hears the published notice in `Desk notices` within the published live delay.

Check-in and check-out by shortcut.
`I` and `O` check the current stay in and out from any control in `Reservation timeline`, a check-in before 04:00 belongs to the previous night, and checking out makes the room dirty.

Room board by touch on a phone.
At 375x812 a signed-in housekeeper lands on `Room board` with `Today's stays`, changes a room by tap with targets at least 44 px and hears the result in `Board status`.

Room status moves.
Every status move and role in the published table is allowed or refused exactly as listed, with the published refusal text for every other move.

Housekeeper sees room, dates and status only.
No page, API response or push message open to a housekeeper carries any guest's name, email, phone, ID or balance, and every stay, folio and guest route answers them as not found.

Check-in link by email.
Creating a stay delivers a message to the guest in Mailpit with the published subject and a working link, and resending issues a new link that kills the old one.

Check-in link scope and end.
The link opens only that stay's published fields and form and answers not found with the published page text at the exact end of its lifetime, on completion, on cancellation and whenever the stay stops being booked.

ID photo limits by content.
The photo upload accepts only JPEG or PNG judged by file content, allows exactly the published byte limit, and refuses anything larger or of another type with the published statuses and text.

Stored photo without EXIF, then Received.
The guest sees `Received` only after MinIO confirms the object at the published key, and the stored image decodes with its EXIF data gone.

Desk sees online check-in live.
When a guest completes the form on a phone, a signed-in desk browser shows `Checked in online` on that stay and hears the published notice in `Desk notices` without reload.

When the close opens.
The close is refused until 04:00:00 hotel time on the date after the business date and opens at that instant, at each worked edge in Business rules including both daylight-saving dates, whatever the browser's zone.

Close posts all or nothing.
A successful close posts no-show fees, then each in-house stay's room charge, tax and city tax in room-number order, fixes the day's figures and advances the date once, and any failure leaves nothing changed.

Close blockers stop everything.
A blocked close posts nothing, returns every blocker, and the screen stops on the first blocked row with focus moved there and the published reason in `Close status`.

Close twice posts once.
A double press of `Run close` sends one request, and a replay naming an already-closed date is refused with the published text and leaves every folio unchanged.

No-shows at the close.
A booked stay arriving on the closing date and not checked in becomes `no_show`, pays the published fee as one charge entry, loses its link and frees its nights.

Night Close Sweep.
After the server commits and never before, the desk passes through the published phases, with row stamps in room-number order, tally figures counting to the committed values and the grid moving one night, all finished within the published time, and a reload at any moment shows the same committed amounts.

Second staff screen follows the close.
A front desk browser open during the owner's close moves to the new business date with the same posted amounts and hears the published result in `Close status` within the published live delay.

Cancellation fee edges.
The fee is zero at one second before the published deadline and the first night's total at the deadline and after, posted as one charge entry, at each worked edge in Business rules.

Free or late comes from the server.
With the browser clock set hours away from the hotel's clock, `Cancellation terms` shows exactly the state the API returns.

Cancel a stay from the panel.
The clerk opens `Cancel stay` from `Stay` by keyboard, reads the fee, confirms and hears the published notice, after which the block shows `cancelled`, the room is free and the guest's link is dead.

Exact folio splits.
Splitting one charge by percent gives each folio its share rounded down with remainder cents placed by the published rule, the shares add up exactly to the charge, and each worked example in Business rules holds.

Split a folio by keyboard.
Using only the keyboard the clerk opens `Split charge`, enters percentages, reads `Split preview`, applies it with focus held inside the dialog and returned to the opener, and hears the result in `Folio status`.

Payments, reversals and balances.
Balance is charges less payments, a correction is a reversal entry referencing the original, and no entry is ever edited or deleted.

Move entries between folios.
Moving an entry changes only the folio it sits on and keeps the stay's total across folios exact.

Folio closes only at zero.
Closing a folio with a balance or without entries is refused with the published text and leaves it open.

Gapless invoices with published PDF lines.
Closing a folio issues the hotel's next number in one per-hotel series, and the stored PDF carries each published text line with amounts equal to the folio's.

Email invoice marks Sent after acceptance.
`Email invoice` delivers a message to the payer in Mailpit with the published subject and the PDF attached, and `Sent` appears only after the mail provider accepts it.

PDF service outage and recovery.
With Gotenberg unreachable, closing a folio shows the published text and status, consumes no number and leaves the folio open, and the same action succeeds with the next number once the service is reachable, with no restart.

File store outage and recovery.
With MinIO unreachable, invoice storage and photo upload show their published text and status with nothing half-saved, and the same action succeeds once the store is reachable, with no restart.

Mail outage and recovery.
With the mail service unreachable, a stay is still created but its link reads as not sent, an invoice stays `Not sent`, each shows the published text, and retrying succeeds once the service is reachable.

Move from a chosen night.
A move from a chosen night keeps earlier nights on the old room as a separate block and moves that night and later, with nightly prices unchanged.

In-house moves keep posted charges.
Moving an in-house guest, from the business date when no night is chosen, requires a clean or inspected target, makes the room left dirty, and leaves every posted entry with the room number it was posted for.

Room moves reach other staff live.
A second signed-in staff browser shows a move's new blocks, room chips and later-posted charges and hears the published notice within the published live delay.

Guest merge field rules.
An empty survivor field takes the other value, a differing field takes the choice made, defaulting to the survivor's, and `Merge conflicts` shows both values with one radio group per differing field.

Merge guests by keyboard.
Using only the keyboard the user completes `Merge guests`, hears the published notice, finds stays and folios on the survivor and issued invoices unchanged, and the merged profile answers not found.

Published report figures.
Occupancy, average daily rate and revenue per available room follow the published formulas and rounding with out-of-order rooms, cancelled stays, no-shows and fees treated as published, including the worked example and the zero case.

Reports update live.
An owner's open `Reports` screen changes its figures without reload within the published live delay after a stay changes in another browser.

Close under reduced motion.
When the device asks for reduced motion, the close shows the final grid, final figures, new date and `Close results` in one step with the same announcement, no ground change and no count or slide.

Sign-in, roles and hotel isolation.
Signed-out callers, other hotels' records and routes barred to the caller's role follow the one published error order and page-route rules, and no response ever crosses from one hotel to another.

Grading setup and clock.
The two grading routes behave as published, including the not-found answer to a wrong key, independent clocks per hotel and every server time rule reading the hotel's clock.

Health and boot without services.
The health route answers as published, the app starts with any provider unreachable, and each provider is read per call.

Published layouts at each viewport.
At 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 each role gets its published layout, order and panel state with no horizontal page overflow, and closed panels are hidden and inert.

Server boundary.
The server applies the published origin rule and size limits, serves no source files or credentials, and keeps the bucket's objects reachable only through the app.

Ledgered nocturnal desk look.
The desk shows hairline rules between room rows, a fixed key-rack column, tabular amounts aligned on the decimal, a full-width tally rail, the built-in serif and sans-serif, and the published colour roles at AA contrast.

Real wiring in the source.
Credentials and service addresses come from the environment, and invoice, photo and mail states come from real provider calls with no hard-coded or simulated results.
`/app/run.json` exists with the string fields `install`, `build`, `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`.
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at `/app` lists every shipped package with its licence, where shipped packages means the production dependency tree (`npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`).

Shipped packages use only the licences MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, 0BSD, MPL-2.0, BlueOak-1.0.0, CC0-1.0, Unlicense or LGPL-3.0-or-later, judged on the production dependency tree (`npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`).
The app uses only Postgres, MinIO, Mailpit and Gotenberg, with no other datastore, broker or hosted service.
The app loads no font, image, script or stylesheet from another origin, and ships no font files.
The provided service configuration and environment values stay as supplied, and no credential appears in the source.
